paper_title: Every good regulator is a model: what Conant and Ashby mean for AI systems that run themselves
paper_frame: Conant and Ashby argued that the best possible regulator of a system must be, in effect, a model of that system. An AI system that runs a business without an explicit model of its own parts is regulating blind. We check whether this system keeps such a model: a knowledge graph of its own data, declared limits for what it must hold steady, and work items specific enough to be checked.
title: Every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system
institution: International Journal of Systems Science, vol. 1, no. 2, pp. 89-97
data: Theorem with proof, in information-theoretic terms.
summary: Under broad conditions, the simplest regulator that achieves the best outcome is one whose actions are a mapping of the regulated system's states. In plain terms: to control something well you must model it, and the quality of control is bounded by the quality of the model.
limits: The theorem is about optimal and simplest regulators. We use it as a design rule, not as proof that this system's model is good enough.
The graph reading counts systems whose graph is built; it does not measure how faithful each graph is.

misperception.belief: An AI agent can manage a system it has no explicit model of, because the model is in its weights.
misperception.short: The model is in the weights.
misperception.counter: A regulator is only as good as its model of the thing it regulates. A system that runs itself needs an explicit, current model of its own parts, kept as data it can read and check.

findings.concern: A regulator with no model of the regulated system
findings.claim: Each system the platform runs should keep a model of its own data. Here that is the knowledge graph each system builds from its own tables.

mechanisms.how: every table becomes graph nodes and edges, kept each pass
every system has a row, built or pending

findings.concern: A model with no stated outcomes to hold
findings.claim: The theorem measures a regulator by the outcomes it keeps. A model is useless for regulation unless the outcomes it serves are declared with limits.

findings.concern: Work items too vague to map to a state
findings.claim: If the regulator's actions are a mapping of system states, each action has to name the state it changes and how to check it. A work item without a done check and a live probe is an action mapped to nothing.

mechanisms.how: fails items with no done check, prediction, out-of-scope line or live probe
